title: Paper Towels 6-roll

drivers.name: week after promotion (20% off)
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted effect of prior post-promo weeks is x0.79, but only 15 sightings; prior promotion was moderate (20% off), not deep; recent sales (187) are near baseline; evidence is thin, so shrink effect toward 1.0.

adjustment.analysis: No events or price change this week. The baseline already reflects recent trends and seasonality. The classical uplift model suggests a 21% dip due to the week after a promotion, but the prior promotion (20% off on 2026-04-13) was only 2 weeks ago, and the noise-adjusted effect of such weeks is x0.79. However, the 2026-04-13 promotion was not a deep discount (20% off), and the post-promo effect is uncertain. The evidence is thin, and the past week’s sales (187 units) are close to baseline. No driver justifies moving the median. Shrink the uplift model’s suggestion toward 1.0 due to limited evidence and noise. Spread remains unchanged.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-18% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
